shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-downward-jump-h.why: The mathematics matches Step 1 of the record. Restricting to delta > 1 is legitimate, since the identity h^2 = tau^(2-2 delta) and the mean-value bound (tau+h)^delta - (tau-h)^delta <= 2h delta (tau+h)^(delta-1) both need delta >= 1. The defect is attribution. The record names the problem only as arXiv:2607.07410, Remark 5.3(ii). It gives no authors ('Yuichi Shiozawa and Jian Wang') and no title ('Essential spectrum for Brox-type diffusion processes'), so neither can be checked against the record. Remove them unless they are verified independently.
shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-downward-jump-h.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_criterion_controlled_against_the_papers_own_deterministic_benchmark] This is a local estimate used in the campaign answer to the first case (w_1 = |x|^delta) of the open question in Remark 5.3(ii) of arXiv:2607.07410. Fix delta > 1 and x_0 > 0. Let V be a real, locally bounded, cadlag function on (0,infinity), and set B_l(x) = (integral_{x_0}^x exp(y^delta+V(y)) dy)(integral_x^infinity exp(-y^delta-V(y)) dy), allowing an infinite product. Suppose V has a downward jump of size m > 0 at a sufficiently large time tau, so V(tau-) - V(tau) = m. Put h = min(tau^(1-delta),1), assume tau-h > x_0, and define O_1 = sup_{tau-h<=y<tau}|V(y)-V(tau-)| and O_2 = sup_{tau<=y<=tau+h}|V(y)-V(tau)|. Then B_l(tau) >= exp(-4 delta) tau^(2-2 delta) exp(m-O_1-O_2). So the logarithmic cost of a quiet well at tau is (2 delta-2) log tau, while its jump depth contributes m. The bound uses only the integrals over [tau-h,tau] and [tau,tau+h], so it holds with x_0 replaced by any R < tau-h. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-confining-diffu.why: Four points. (1) The hypothesis delta > max(1,1/alpha) does not match the written proof. The proof needs h_k = 2^(k(1-delta)) -> 0, so that e^{-6h_k lambda_1} >= 1/2 and Q(osc_{[0,6h_k]} V' > 1/2) -> 0, and it needs h^2 = tau^(2-2 delta). Both require only delta > 1; nothing in the proof uses delta > 1/alpha. The draft's own justification, 'the shrinking-window range', is exactly delta > 1. The correct range is therefore delta > 1, which also covers (1, 1/alpha] when alpha < 1. (2) The record's headline claim of 'every delta' is not delivered by the written proof for delta <= 1, because h_k = 1 there and the window does not shrink. For delta <= 1/alpha the conclusion is the paper's Proposition 5.2. That leaves alpha in (1,2) with delta in (1/alpha, 1] unproved, so the entry correctly does not claim all delta. (3) The author names and paper title are not in the record. (4) Minor constant slip in the record's proof: the two factors that are each >= 1/2 give 6 h_k c_* m_k^(-alpha)/4 = 1.5 h_k c_* m_k^(-alpha), not 3 h_k c_* m_k^(-alpha). The conclusion is unaffected. The proof text otherwise reproduces the record, including a dangling reference to 'the numerical section below'.
shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-confining-diffu.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_criterion_controlled_against_the_papers_own_deterministic_benchmark] This is the proved range of the campaign answer to the first case (w_1 = |x|^delta) of the open question in Remark 5.3(ii) of arXiv:2607.07410. Let Q denote the law of a two-sided, nontrivial, (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process V with cadlag paths and V(0)=0, where alpha is in (0,2), Q(V(1)>0)>0 and Q(V(1)<0)>0. Strictly alpha-stable processes are included. Let nu be its Levy measure and suppose nu((-infinity,0)) > 0. Let delta > 1. Put w(x) = |x|^delta + V(x) and mu^w(dx) = exp(-w(x))dx. Let L^w be the self-adjoint operator associated with the closure on L^2(R,mu^w) of E^w(f,f) = (1/2) integral_R |f'(x)|^2 exp(-w(x))dx, f in C_c^infinity(R). For any fixed x_0 > 0 define B_l(x) = (integral_{x_0}^x exp(w(y))dy)(integral_x^infinity exp(-w(y))dy). Then, Q-almost surely: limsup_{x->infinity} B_l(x) = infinity, and this holds with x_0 replaced by any R; the bottom lambda_ess of the essential spectrum of -L^w is 0; and the semigroup exp(tL^w) is noncompact. For 0 < delta <= 1/alpha the same conclusion is the paper's Proposition 5.2. The record's claim for alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 is not covered by the written proof. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-outward-diffusi.why: The reduction is checked and correct. Replacing V by -V turns positive jumps into negative ones, and B_l for |x|^delta - V equals B_r for -|x|^delta + V. The w, density and B_r conventions in the draft are consistent. The remaining defects are the same as in the previous entry. The proof establishes delta > 1, not delta > max(1,1/alpha); the delta <= 1/alpha range is the paper's Proposition 5.2; and alpha in (1,2) with delta in (1/alpha,1] is not covered. The author names and title are absent from the record.
shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-outward-diffusi.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_criterion_controlled_against_the_papers_own_deterministic_benchmark] This is the proved range of the campaign answer to the second case (w_2 = -|x|^delta) of the open question in Remark 5.3(ii) of arXiv:2607.07410. Let Q denote the law of a two-sided, nontrivial, (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process V with cadlag paths and V(0)=0, where alpha is in (0,2), Q(V(1)>0)>0 and Q(V(1)<0)>0. Strictly alpha-stable processes are included. Let nu be its Levy measure and suppose nu((0,infinity)) > 0. Let delta > 1. Put w(x) = -|x|^delta + V(x) and mu^w(dx) = exp(-w(x))dx. Let L^w be the self-adjoint operator associated with the closure on L^2(R,mu^w) of E^w(f,f) = (1/2) integral_R |f'(x)|^2 exp(-w(x))dx, f in C_c^infinity(R). For fixed x_0 > 0 set B_r(x) = (integral_x^infinity exp(w(y))dy)(integral_{x_0}^x exp(-w(y))dy). Then, Q-almost surely: limsup_{x->infinity} B_r(x) = infinity; lambda_ess(-L^w) = 0; and exp(tL^w) is noncompact. The proof is the negative-jump calculation applied to -V, with the two Hardy factors interchanged. For 0 < delta <= 1/alpha the same conclusion is the paper's Proposition 5.2. The record's claim for alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 is not covered by the written proof. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-jump-sign-dicho.why: This entry is mostly faithful. It keeps the all-delta claim as a report, and it correctly labels Theorem 3 as a sketch with the uniform near-field estimate unwritten. Its densities exp(-|x|^delta - V) and exp(|x|^delta - V) are correct for w_1+V and w_2+V. The caveat that compactness at one end is not compactness of the operator matches open problem 3. Three corrections are needed. (1) The retained proof range is delta > 1, not delta > max(1,1/alpha). (2) The remaining coverage should be stated: delta <= 1/alpha is the paper's Proposition 5.2, and alpha in (1,2) with delta in (1/alpha,1] is not covered by the written proof. (3) The author names and title are not in the record. Also, Theorem 3 assumes alpha > 1, so max(1,1/alpha) = 1 there; this is harmless.
shiozawa-wang-remark-5-3-jump-sign-dicho.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_criterion_controlled_against_the_papers_own_deterministic_benchmark] This is the broader partial answer reported for both cases of the open question in Remark 5.3(ii) of arXiv:2607.07410. Let V be a two-sided (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process with alpha in (0,2), whose value at time one has positive probability of each sign, and let nu be its Levy measure. For delta > 0 consider the two diffusion forms with reference densities exp(-|x|^delta - V(x)) and exp(|x|^delta - V(x)), each with energy (1/2) integral |f'|^2 times the corresponding density. The record claims noncompactness, with essential-spectrum bottom zero, for every delta, when nu has negative jumps in the first case or positive jumps in the second. The written quiet-window proof covers delta > 1; the paper's Proposition 5.2 covers 0 < delta <= 1/alpha. Together these give all delta when alpha <= 1, which includes alpha < 1, where nu must charge both half-lines. For alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 the claim is not established by the written argument. For alpha > 1, delta > 1 and no negative jumps, the record also sketches compactness at the +infinity end of the first diffusion via the bound B_l(x) <= C^2 x^(2-2delta). Here B_l is the integral of the reciprocal density from a fixed positive x_0 to x times the integral of the density from x to infinity, and C is a finite path-dependent constant. The record explicitly leaves the uniform near-field estimate unwritten, so this converse is a sketch. Compactness at one end does not by itself establish compactness of the full two-sided operator. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
